prompt: Why is deleting a node Θ(1) in a doubly linked list but Θ(n) in a singly linked list (given only a pointer to the node)?
options: Doubly linked lists are always shorter
A doubly linked list's prev pointer avoids walking from the head to find the predecessor
Singly linked lists don't support deletion
explanation: With a prev pointer, you can directly relink the predecessor and successor. Without it, you must scan from the head to find the predecessor first.

prompt: What is the main purpose of a sentinel node in a linked list implementation?
explanation: A sentinel provides a permanent dummy head/tail so every real node always has a valid neighbor, removing the need to special-case empty lists or boundaries.

prompt: [Real 2025 exam question] Which statement about linked lists is correct?
options: Inserting two elements consecutively at the end of a singly linked list (no tail pointer) requires at most two traversals of the list.
Every element in a singly linked list contains at least two pointers.
Singly linked lists allow direct indexed access to an arbitrary element.
You can iterate backwards through a singly linked list.
explanation: Without a tail pointer, each append walks from head to the end — one traversal per insert, so two inserts cost at most two traversals. A singly linked node has only one pointer (next), no index access, and no backward iteration.

prompt: [Real 2025 exam question] Which two statements are correct?
options: An advantage of linked lists is that insert/delete can be done by simply adjusting pointers, without shifting the remaining elements.
In a doubly linked list, each element holds a pointer only to the next element.
An abstract data type (ADT) describes the possible values, operations, and behavior of a data type, but not its concrete implementation.
The ADT description specifies the time complexity of operations on linked lists.
explanation: Doubly linked lists have both next and prev pointers. An ADT is implementation-agnostic by definition — complexity depends on the concrete implementation chosen, not the ADT spec.
